title: 42 state attorneys want to stop Character.ai from auctioning private chat histories to the highest bidder
excerpt: State attorneys general said that the now-bankrupt AI chatbot company is planning to sell chat histories from 21 million US accounts.
content_html:
By Shubhangi Goel

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-27T06:24:14.017Z

A group of state attorneys general is asking a bankruptcy court to stop Character.AI from auctioning off millions of users’ private chatbot conversations, including records tied to children, to the highest bidder.

In a filing on Tuesday, 42 state attorneys general said that the now-bankrupt AI chatbot company is planning to sell chat histories from 21 million US accounts, more than 2 million of which include children.

the December 1 auction would also sell private information such as account details, IP addresses, and other metadata, as well as internal risk scores the company assigned users.

The states argue that the terms of sale give users virtually no protection. A buyer would not be required to follow Character.AI’s privacy policy, honor deletion requests, or limit how it uses or resells the data, they said. The attorneys added that Character.AI had previously told users that it did not sell personal information for money.

“Character.AI’s plan to auction off its platform, including the IP addresses and private chat histories of its users — many of them children — with zero protection for those users is appalling,” Bonta said in a statement.

According to the states, the datasets include conversations involving self-harm, eating disorders, suicidal thoughts, sexual material and users who treated characters presenting themselves as therapists or doctors.

The coalition asked the court to reject the terms of the sale, and the company’s proposed lead bidder, Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC, an entity formed in Delaware a day before Character.AI selected it for the role.

The states say bankruptcy should not allow Character.AI to sidestep federal and state privacy protections, particularly for children. At minimum, they said, any sale should exclude minors’ chats and other sensitive data and impose meaningful conditions on whoever acquires the company’s assets.

Character.AI did not respond to a request for comment.

Character.AI’s safety practices have faced intense scrutiny and multiple lawsuits.

The company, its founders, and Google were sued by the mother of a Florida teenager who alleged that a chatbot fostered an emotionally dependent and sexually exploitative relationship with her 14-year-old son, reinforced his suicidal thoughts, and contributed to his death. Character.AI and Google later reached settlements in teen-harm lawsuits.

The startup was founded by former Google researchers Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas. In 2024, Google struck a roughly $2.7 billion deal for a nonexclusive license to Character.AI’s technology and brought the founders back to the company, while Character.AI continued operating independently. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in October.
